newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German October state inflation.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German October state inflation.

text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' comments in reaction to the release of state inflation data from Hesse and Baden-Wuerttemberg. Hesse said consumer prices rose 1.3 percent year-on-year and were unchanged month-on-month in October, compared with September's 1.2 percent and down 0.1 percent, respectively. Baden-Wuerttemberg said prices were unchanged on the month and rose 1.3 percent on the year, compared with down 0.2 percent on the month and up 1.2 percent on the year a month earlier.
GERHARD GREBE, chief economist at Bank Julius Baer in Frankfurt: "Higher mineral oil prices helped push rates up."
"It appears that pressure from oil prices and the weaker mark has been overcompensated by vacation and rent costs. The figures are fully on target," said Preuschl.
ELANIE HELDMANN, BfG Bank in Frankfurt: "The inflation figures from the states count as a positive result, a little bit higher than we expected.
"The prices are favorable particularly if you look at energy prices -- heating oil prices have gone much higher, but still the overall energy figure is only moderately higher," said Heldmann.

"The 1.8-percent figure for rents in Baden-Wuerttemberg is above average, but all in all, the figures suggest a decent price environment. It leaves the Bundesbank in a good position to leave rates where they are. There is no real reason for a cut in short-term interest rates. All in all, a positive development," said Heldmann.
